Kinh Duong Vuong
[1b] His taboo name was Loc Tuc, a descendant of the Than Nong clan.
Year of Nham Tuat, 17th year. In the past, De Minh, the third-generation descendant of Viem De of the Than Nong clan, fathered De Nghi. Lac Long Quan
[2a] His taboo name was Sung Lam, son of Kinh Duong Vuong.
The king married De Lai's daughter, Au Co, and fathered a hundred sons (legend has it she gave birth to a hundred eggs), who are the ancestors of the Bach Viet. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

{"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production
Rihanna with red, long hair and a dress with floral patterns. Her left hand is raised and her right-hand holds a microphone near her mouth.
Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Recording
Mike Strange recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan.[19] The sessions took two days.[20] Strange edited the vocals with D-Verb—a reverberation software—and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make few changes; for "Love the Way You Lie" he almost exclusively used board compression and console equalization. Strange used the Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools for "brighter" reverberation. Detroit musician Luis Resto has contributed to the arrangement on many of Eminem's songs, but did not do so for "Love the Way You Lie". According to Strange, "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals."[2] Two to three weeks after the sessions, Alex da Kid arrived to help mix and master the track.[11] He wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it.[3] Strange said, "It was simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid]'d sent us."[2] Strange's brother Joe engineered the track.[19]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. The R&B songwriter Makeba Riddick provided additional vocal production.[19] Strange used equalization, compression and reverberation but left the vocal balance. He assumed that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes on her seven stereo vocal tracks.[2]
